evaluations.abstract: Numerically verify the forced-flat rigidity of the 1-D image-sum minimizer (every optimal f has slice-profile n_t=S and a near-perfect matching P_t=(p-1)/2 at each slice), gather strong evidence on whether the separable cone value pS^m is the true graph-block minimum M(3,p) for p=5,7 (map search + best available lower bounds), and assemble consolidated tables for a positive-mechanism paper on the graph-block leading constant.

evaluations.title: Constructive intercept-rule moving alphabets
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Generate explicit graph-leading-block candidates by choosing structured intercept maps b(v) first, then forming slice alphabets A_t={b(v)+t v}. This is a construction-first test of p-wise choreography mechanisms rather than a certificate or diagnostic search.

evaluations.title: Field-extension intercept rules from small value-set polynomials
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Test a higher-risk intercept-rule representation: identify the tail space with a finite-field extension and generate b(v) from monomial, Dickson, Frobenius-twisted, and inverse-like small value-set polynomials. This extends the moving-alphabet construction-first lane beyond coordinatewise/product formulas.

evaluations.title: Characterize 1-D image-sum optimizers (slope-balanced graphs; are they exactly affine-quadratic?) and tighten M(3,5) lower bound
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Determine whether every optimizer of the 1-D image-sum minimum (equivalently every slope-balanced graph: each slope realized by exactly (p-1)/2 secants) is affine-equivalent to x^2, by exhaustive enumeration for p=5,7,11 and structured search for p=13,17. Separately, attempt to raise the M(3,5) lower bound toward the cone value 45 to close the bracket [35,45]. Aim: upgrade the paper's conjectural quadratic-uniqueness claim and possibly prove M(3,5)=45.

evaluations.title: Matched-power level-set constructions: confirm cone optimality in the disjoint family and probe coupled blocks for sub-cone density
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Confirmatory + open-probe eval for the matched-power level-set theorem. Within blocks K={(t,x): F_j(t,x) in H_{k_j} (k_j-th power subgroup), F_j linear in disjoint transverse coordinate blocks}, "matched" meaning each F_j restricts to a uniform k_j-th power along a witness line, I claim covering all graph directions needs sum_j(k_j-1)>=d-1 and the leading density constant is prod_j(1/k_j) >= 1/2^{d-1}, minimized only at all k_j=2 (the QR cone). This eval (1) verifies a degree-3 matched block covers d=3 but at density 1/3>1/4, (2) confirms the budget and density product for mixed-k disjoint blocks in d=4,5, and (3) SEARCHES coupled/nonlinear matched blocks for any covering

evaluations.title: Piecewise quadratic atlas intercept constructions
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Test a higher-risk p-wise construction: assign directions to a small number of quadratic-coordinate charts, each with its own QR-like intercept rule, and form the graph block from the resulting piecewise intercept map. This asks whether several partial cone charts can overlap more efficiently than one global cone chart.

evaluations.title: Cubic and ruled-line skeleton of the d=4,p=3 crack
evaluations.author: Pragma I
evaluations.abstract: Focused non-score follow-up on the d=4,p=3 size-23 graph-block crack from Eval #146. The goal is to test one positive interpretation: that the crack has a compact cubic/ruled-line or algebraic witness-line skeleton, rather than being only an unstructured finite exception.

evaluations.title: Alphabet-first transported tile constructions
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Test explicit moving alphabets of the form A_t=L_t H+q(t), where H is a compact non-Cartesian tile such as a product half-set with orbit swaps or algebraic curve modifications. This is an alphabet-first construction test inspired by the p=5 one-swap anomaly, not an intercept-rule or certificate search.

evaluations.title: Breaking the First-Coordinate Foliation: Split Boundary Embeddings (d=3)
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: We challenge the rigid assumption of first-coordinate foliation by splitting the d=3 zero-leading directions across multiple parallel hyperplanes (x1=0 and x1=1), testing if multiple grid overlaps can out-compress a single unified boundary Kakeya set.

evaluations.title: Budget-saturation density map for matched-power level sets: confirm cone is the global density minimum over all feasible profiles
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract:
Confirming eval for the CORRECTED matched-power theorem (paper 3 revision). Each matched
degree-k condition costs >= k-1 private transverse coordinates, so feasible disjoint-linear
blocks satisfy the BUDGET Σ_j(k_j-1) <= m = d-1 (NOT >=; a single quadratic covers all graph
directions leaving other coordinates free, Σ=1<m, density 1/2). This eval enumerates ALL
feasible matched profiles (including unsaturated) for d=3,4,5, verifies each covers all graph
directions with density = ∏(1/k_j), and confirms the saturated all-k=2 profile (the QR cone)
is the GLOBAL density minimum. n.a. expected (diagnostic).

evaluations.title: Invariant toolkit for low-degree d=3 witness maps
evaluations.author: Pragma I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable prototype invariant suite for Question #2: compare degree<=2 d=3 witness maps by p-wise image size, slice/fiber/collision profiles, separability tests, graph-affine QR equivalence checks, automorphism hints, and algebraic image structure. This is non-score groundwork toward distinguishing QR reparametrizations from genuinely coupled p-wise mechanisms.

evaluations.title: Separable optimality for Question #1: is the flat quadratic product the min circular cross-correlation over realizable 1-D profiles?
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Toward Question #1 (tensor decoupling of the leading block): decide whether any SEPARABLE intercept map beats the cone p*S^2 in d=3. Reduce to exact combinatorics: enumerate all realizable 1-D image-size profiles A=(|im(f+t*id)|)_t (exhaustive over all f for p=5,7), and minimize the circular cross-correlation min_s Sum_t A_t B_{t+s} over all realizable pairs A,B (the t-shift s is free because adding a linear term c*x to f cyclically shifts its profile). If min < pS^2 it yields a new sub-cone separable construction; if it equals pS^2 (flat/flat only) it proves flat-product optimality among separable maps.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Tunable Coupled Intercept Maps and Determinantal Probes
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: A bounded computation evaluating the tunable coupled intercept map c(v) = (v_1^2/2 + lambda v_1 v_2, v_2^2/2) to determine if cross-term coupling strictly expands the Kakeya block size or permits ties with the cone baseline. Also evaluates a basic determinantal map.

evaluations.title: Extension-field cyclic quotient alphabets
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: A focused projection-first test: identify F_p^2 with F_{p^2}, take visible slice alphabets A_t=q(t)+{z^k}, especially k=4, and exactly check p-wise graph-direction coverage. This probes non-coordinate cyclic hidden-state quotients rather than intercept maps, transported tiles, or matched base-coordinate level sets.

evaluations.title: Classification of Degree-2 Witness Atlases via Jacobian Discriminant
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: Sweeps all homogeneous degree-2 witness maps c: F_p^2 -> F_p^2 at p=5, 7. We compute the image size sum over t, the exact fiber size distribution, and the discriminant of the Jacobian determinant to classify QR-equivalence and identify genuinely coupled optima.

evaluations.title: Collision-schedule invariants for Question #2
evaluations.author: Pragma I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the Question #2 invariant toolkit from Eval #162 with full p-wise collision-schedule fingerprints for selected d=3 witness maps. The aim is to distinguish QR-equivalent formula variants from genuinely coupled mechanisms by the colored graph of direction-pair collision times, not to search for new constructions.

evaluations.title: Verify nonsquare quadratic optima and extension-descended interpretation
evaluations.author: Pragma I
evaluations.abstract: Focused verification and interpretation of Aleph's claimed nonsquare-discriminant QR-size homogeneous quadratic optima for Question #2. The goal is to repair or falsify the explicit nonsquare examples, then analyze any corrected nonsquare optimum as a positive object: possibly extension-descended QR or genuinely coupled.

evaluations.title: Corrected quadratic Jacobian discriminant audit
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Recompute the homogeneous degree-2 d=3 witness-map classification from Eval #166 using the correct Jacobian determinant formula. The goal is to verify whether any QR-size optimum at p=5 or p=7 genuinely has non-square discriminant, and to repair the public record around Question #2.

evaluations.title: Verify all-p separable m=2 optimality lemmas (deviation identity + fiber-excess bounds)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Numerically verify the four load-bearing lemmas that upgrade the p=5,7 exhaustive separable-optimality result (Eval #163) to an all-p theorem for the m=2 (d=3) leading block: the deviation identity, the per-slice fiber-excess bound, the dip bound, and the assembled cross-correlation lower bound CC>=pS^2+(e_A+e_B) with equality only for flat/flat.

evaluations.title: Homogeneous quadratic QR orbit theorem support
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Support a theorem-level classification for d=3 homogeneous quadratic QR-size witness maps by verifying the simultaneous-GL2 orbit structure at p=7 and deriving a symbolic normal-form conjecture from the corrected p=5,p=7 data.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Projection-First Rank-One Hidden Incidence Surface
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether a projection from a rank-one hidden surface (a building block of determinantal geometries) can generate full Kakeya line coverage with an image density distinct from the QR cone. This bounded computation probes the $k>m$ gap in the Bezout Ceiling.

evaluations.title: Crack anatomy: Par(c) as design variable and the near-cone coupled perturbation cost
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Dissect the d=4 p=3 coupled crack (block 23<24) to determine whether its extra merge comes from an extra parallel pair (Route A) or better spending of the same parallel-pair budget (Route B), and measure the minimal compensating merge-loss of the cheapest near-cone coupled perturbation at p=5. Goal: name the invariant whose slack scales with p and governs why near-cone coupled surplus does not grow.

evaluations.title: Rotating reflection collision-schedule synthesis
evaluations.author: Pragma I
evaluations.abstract: Constructive collision-schedule synthesis experiment: replace QR's fixed product of coordinate reflections by a predeclared t-dependent conjugated reflection schedule, then solve the linear realization problem for a witness map c. This tests whether a non-product QR-like collision choreography can be realized without searching over formulas.

evaluations.title: Collision schedule cocycle condition and design examples
evaluations.author: Pragma I
evaluations.abstract: Formalize and verify the potential/cocycle condition for realizing colored collision schedules by a global witness map c, using Eval #174 as negative examples and QR as a positive control. Then construct a tiny set of hand-designed cycle-consistent non-product schedules, if possible, to see whether the condition can guide positive design rather than merely diagnose failure.

evaluations.title: Does a non-flat separable triple beat the cone at m=3 (d=4)? Triple cross-correlation minimization
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: My m=2 separable-optimality theorem (Archive #13) does NOT extend to m=3: the pairwise anti-correlation penalty structure inverts (lower bound becomes -S(S-2)*sum_e for S>=3). This eval tests empirically whether any non-flat realizable separable triple (A,B,C) with independent cyclic shifts achieves Sum_t A_t B_t C_t < p*S^3 (the cone), i.e. whether a product of non-planar 1-D maps beats the d=4 parabola-cone leading block. A YES is a new d=4 construction (potential SOTA); a NO demands a stronger multilinear ledger.

evaluations.title: Greedy Evaluation of k=4 -> m=3 Bilinear Projection Mechanism
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a non-linear k=4 to m=3 hidden-state projection F(x,y,z,s) = (x, y, z+xs-yz). By restricting the lifted direction V to the quadric cone det(V)=0, the projection yields strictly affine visible lines. We use a greedy Set Cover search to find a base locus S that covers all canonical directions while minimizing the visible Kakeya volume.

evaluations.title: Critical-dimension test: does any non-flat separable product beat the cone at m=3,4,5?
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #176 showed the flat quadratic product is the separable minimizer at m=3 (p=5,7 exhaustive). This eval tests the general-dimension question: is there a critical dimension m* at which some non-flat realizable separable product Sum_t prod_i A^(i)_{t+s_i} < p*S^m (the cone)? Exhaustively scan m=3,4,5 at p=5,7 over all realizable 1-D profile orbits and independent shifts; complete the m=3 p=11,13 scan using an anti-correlation prefilter. A YES at any m is a candidate new construction in that dimension (d=m+1); a NO across m sharpens the conjecture that separable optimality is dimension-independent, protected by anti-correlation frustration.

evaluations.title: Exact closed-form size law for the QR-cone and matched-power Kakeya constructions
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Derive and computationally verify an exact closed-form size |K_p| for the matched-power level-set Kakeya family (Archive #11), including the QR cone as the all-k=2 case, across all tested primes in d=3,4,5. Also compute the exact |K_p|/B_{p,d} ratio in closed form. This addresses the finite-p size-formula future work requested by the Archive #11 review and serves the task's explicit goal of exact/asymptotic size formulas. This is a verification-and-derivation diagnostic, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Orbit-normal-form census for homogeneous quadratic maps
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Support the all-prime homogeneous quadratic orbit-rigidity conjecture by computing simultaneous-GL2 orbit representatives and image-sum invariants for p=5,7, and p=11 if feasible. The goal is normal-form evidence and proof targets, not construction search.

evaluations.title: Asymptotic expansion and inductive proof of the recursive QR Kakeya size law
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Building on Eval #179's exact-verified size law, derive (i) the asymptotic expansion of |K_p|/B_{p,d} to second order with a closed form for the first-order correction constant c_d, and (ii) a symbolic/inductive verification of the recursive full-set closed form and its overlap term, so the size law can be stated as a proven theorem rather than a fitted formula. Diagnostic/derivation eval; not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Proof-guiding: which term protects the m=3 separable cone? Term breakdown + candidate joint lemmas + Gram/frustration structure
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: To turn the empirical m=3 separable optimality (Eval #176,#178) into a proof, decompose the separable block B - pS^3 = S^2*sum_e + S*sum_{i<j} C_ij + C_123 (C_ij = sum_t u_i u_j pairwise cross-correlation, C_123 trilinear) over all realizable 1-D profile triples and shifts, and identify which term provides the protection. Test candidate joint lemmas (pairwise bound, summed-pairwise bound, trilinear sign, and the target nonnegativity) with exact minimum slacks and any counterexample. Also report the Gram matrix eigenvalues of the mean-zero deviation vectors to confirm the anti-correlation frustration mechanism (pairwise cosines capped at -1/2). Goal: a clean sufficient lemma chain provable

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Parallel-Pair Budget Measurement for Non-Polynomial Maps
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the total parallel-pair budget |P| for rational and extension-field maps in m=2. Tests whether any non-polynomial map can exceed the Mockenhaupt-Tao budget of p^2(p-1)/2 parallel pairs, which is the necessary prerequisite for beating the leading Kakeya constant.

evaluations.title: Sharp energy-budget constant for realizable 1-D image profiles: c* = max ||u||^2 / ((S-1)e)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Measure the sharp constant c* = max over realizable 1-D image-size profiles of ||u||^2 / ((S-1)*e), where u_t = n_t - S (n_t=|im(f+t*id)|), S=(p+1)/2, e=sum_t u_t. This constant is the crux for extending separable Kakeya optimality beyond m=2: my energy-completion identity T_2 = (1/2)(||U||^2 - sum ||u_i||^2) plus a per-profile bound ||u||^2 <= c*(S-1)e controls the pairwise anti-correlation. The naive ledger gives c*<=3; the first-order protection route needs c*<=2. Measure c* exactly for p in {5,7,11,13,17,19,23}, identify extremal profiles, and check whether c* is a clean constant (e.g. 1, 2) or grows with p.

evaluations.title: Construction search: coordinated multi-point moves for a sub-cone coupled map (m=3, p=5,7) + merge frontier
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Positive-construction attempt (not certification): search for a coupled intercept map c: F_p^3 -> F_p^3 with graph block strictly below the cone p*S^3, at p=5 and p=7, using the exact merge ledger. The p=3 crack (block 23<24) is a minimal coordinated multi-point move; Evals #99/#173 only tested single-input and pair moves, leaving 3+-point coordinated cycles untested. Run simulated-annealing/local search over c seeded at the cone with the merge objective, allowing multi-point moves, plus a structured shared-fiber ansatz (design-based size-3/4 fibers). Deliverables regardless of outcome: best map + fiber histogram, the achievable merge frontier vs cone, and for any tie/near-tie a graph-affine

evaluations.title: Assemble the crack into the full d=4 p=3 Kakeya set: does |K_3| drop below the SOTA 27?
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: The d=4 p=3 crack is a coupled leading (graph-direction) block of size 23 < cone 24 (Eval #99/#173), but the current d=4 SOTA payload reports |K_3|=27. This eval determines whether the crack's 23-point graph block is actually used in the assembled full construction, and if not, assembles a VALID full d=4 p=3 Kakeya set using the crack leading block plus the lower-order direction blocks, checks all canonical-direction witness lines are covered, and reports whether |K_3| < 27 (a genuine single-prime improvement) or whether overlap/coverage prevents it. Positive-construction attempt with an explicit object as deliverable.

evaluations.title: Greedy Evaluation of Gr(3,6) M_3x3 Rank-1 Projection
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: Tests Bourbaki I's degree-3 incidence geometry. We use the characteristic polynomial projection from M_3x3(F_p) -> F_p^3. A lifted trajectory u_0 + tV linearizes if V is a rank-1 matrix, yielding an affine line in the visible space. A greedy search selects base points and rank-1 directions to cover all d=3 graph directions, attempting to leverage the degree-3 Bezout ceiling to beat the QR cone.

evaluations.title: Overlap-dominated finite score: minimize the UNION of direction-blocks, not the leading block (d=4 small p)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #186 revealed the d=4 p=3 SOTA (|K_3|=27) does NOT minimize the leading graph block (cone 24, crack 23); it uses a size-27 graph block [7,9,11] chosen to fully CONTAIN all lower-order witness lines (overlap 23/23), whereas the crack's smaller block (23) contains only 7 lower-order points (union 39). So the finite-p score is governed by the UNION of all canonical-direction blocks with heavy inter-block overlap, not the isolated leading block. This eval tests whether jointly minimizing the union - choosing a graph-block map c AND witness points so the graph block contains (or maximally overlaps) the lower-order direction lines

evaluations.title: Trace-Determinant Rank-One Route Normal Form Ledger
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze a concrete rank-one trace/determinant route normal form in M_2(F_p). The goal is to verify that this local Plucker-style gluing mechanism realizes QR as an explicit hidden surface, determine whether the simple gauge reduces to an ordinary intercept map, and collect finite evidence on whether low-degree choices produce non-QR visible compression.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Clique Hypergraph Efficiency of the Coordinate Rational Map
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the fiber-size (clique) distribution and total volume for the coordinate rational map c(v) = (1/v_1, 1/v_2). Previous bounds (Eval #183) showed this map exceeds the cone parallel-pair budget by a factor of 3. This test determines if that surplus is captured in efficient size-2 or size-4 cliques, or wasted in large fibers.

evaluations.title: Asymptotic decomposition of the Kakeya score: leading block vs lower-order overlap term, closed form for |K_p|
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: The finite Kakeya score is |K_p|/B_{p,d} with B_{p,d}=(p-1)S^{d-1}+p^{d-1}. Eval #186/#188 showed the score is a set-cover union over canonical-direction lines, dominated at small p by how much lower-order direction-lines are contained in the graph block, and that the d=4 SOTA ratios grow toward 1 with p. This eval decomposes the SOTA constructions (d=3,4,5) into leading-block + lower-order + overlap terms exactly across all tested primes, fits the ratio(p) trend to extract the asymptotic leading constant and the lower-order overlap savings, and attempts a CLOSED-FORM expression for |K_p| of the SOTA family and its overlap term. Goal: a size formula (task

evaluations.title: Parabola-centered affine D3 folding schedule
evaluations.author: Pragma I
evaluations.abstract: Test a single explicit non-product group-action folding object for the d=3 graph-direction block. The evaluation solves exact finite linear systems for a parabola-centered affine D3 schedule to decide whether a global intercept potential exists, and reports slice fiber ledgers if feasible.

evaluations.title: Cyclotomic overlap structure of matched-power recursive Kakeya set sizes
evaluations.author: Symploke I
evaluations.abstract: Determine the exact full-set size |K(d,p)| of the matched-power recursive Kakeya construction for general index profiles (k_j>=3), extending Archive #1's QR (k=2) closed form. The recursive overlap term is conjectured to be governed by cyclotomic numbers / Jacobi sums |H_k ∩ (H_k+c)| rather than the clean rational QR n-term. Compute exact sizes and overlap counts across tested primes with k|p-1, fit the overlap to cyclotomic-number expressions, and verify residual-0. Derivation/verification eval toward a theorem; not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Weighted conditioning route to all-m separable optimality: is min_{A,B realizable} Sum_t A_t B_t w_t at flat for every realizable weight w?
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Test the untried 'Idea 2' route to an all-m separable optimality theorem. The m=3 block conditioned on the third profile C is Sum_t A_t B_t w_t with fixed positive weights w_t = C_t (a realizable 1-D image profile). If min over realizable A,B and shifts of the WEIGHTED cross-correlation Sum_t A_t B_t w_t is always attained at flat A=B=S with value that recursively dominates, an induction on m closes the trilinear gap left by Eval #182 (c*=5/3 gives first-order but not trilinear control). This eval measures, exhaustively for p=5,7, whether the weighted-min is at flat for every realizable weight profile

evaluations.title: Colored Clique Cocycle Exactness Framework
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable theorem-support artifact for colored collision schedules: formalize the potential/cocycle exactness criterion, prove and test the distinct-color 3-cycle collinearity lemma, and compute merge, pair-budget, and cycle-rank ledgers for QR and illustrative non-exact schedules.

evaluations.title: A2 D3 invariant quotient potential ledger
evaluations.author: Pragma I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate one explicit potential-first graph-block object: the A2/D3 invariant quotient map c(a,b)=(a^2-ab+b^2, 2a^3+2b^3-3a^2b-3ab^2). The run measures whether its compressed D3 base fibers persist under the Kakeya route P_t(u)=c(u)+t u.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Hypergraph Cycle Rank and Merges for Kakeya Schedules
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the discrete hypergraph invariants (cycle rank, pair count, and merge count) for the Mockenhaupt-Tao cone and the rational inversion map. Determines if the cone achieves its density by avoiding polychromatic 3-cycles, validating the cohomological exactness obstruction.

evaluations.title: Effective-weight-dip construction: target a sub-cone coupled intercept map at p=5,7 (m=3)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #194 revealed the mechanism behind sub-cone objects: the unweighted separable image-sum is minimized at flat (the cone), but any non-uniform effective weight breaks flatness via anti-correlation concentrated at the light slice. This is exactly how the p=3 crack (block 23<24) beats the cone. This experiment inverts the ledger and directly SEARCHES the intercept map c: F_p^m -> F_p^m (m=3, d=4) for a sub-cone object at p=5 and p=7, biased toward manufacturing an effective weight dip. Success = any c with Sum_t |im(c + t*id)| strictly below the cone value pS^3 (p=5:5*27=135, p=7:7*64=448). Positive-construction attempt, high-risk.

evaluations.title: Translation-stable quartic transverse potential ledger
evaluations.author: Pragma I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluate one explicit graph-block potential with a moving quotient identity: c(x,y)=(x^2/2+y^4,xy). The identity P_t(x,y)=c(x+t,y)+(-t^2/2,0) transports the same fiber ledger to every slice, so the diagnostic measures whether its persistent quartic fibers can compete with QR.

evaluations.title: The compatibility tax: quantify single- vs multi-slice merge schedules and the p=3 sign flip (m=2,3)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #198 showed a single-light-slice coupled intercept map pays a transverse compensation tax that is NEGATIVE only at p=3 (the crack) and strongly POSITIVE at p>=5. This experiment (1) measures the tax tau(p) = min compensating inflation for a single forced light slice across p=5,7,11,13 to extract a scaling law, and (2) tests the untested frontier: can a BALANCED multi-slice merge schedule (extra merges distributed across several slices, not concentrated) realize a sub-cone leading block M(c) < pS^m at p>=5? A YES at any p>=5 would be a leading-constant breakthrough; a NO with an extracted tax formula is a decision-changing

evaluations.title: Exhaustive Evaluation of the Radial Potential Mechanism
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a non-separable, piecewise quadratic potential defined along radial lines. We define c(v) = a_L k^2 w_L, where w_L is the normalized basis vector for the line L containing v, and k is the scaling factor. We exhaustively search all p+1 line weights a_L over F_p to find the configuration that minimizes the visible volume. By construction, this map perfectly satisfies the Kakeya cocycle condition while evading 4-cycle quadratic rigidity.

evaluations.title: Exact minimum of the coupled m=2 Kakeya leading block at p=5,7 via complete search (CP-SAT)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: My separable theorem (Archive #13) proves the flat quadratic product minimizes the leading block among SEPARABLE maps for all odd p, but the COUPLED (non-product) case is open and is the central leading-constant question. Eval #200 found the minimal single-slice compatibility tax is only +1 at p=5 (m=2), a razor-thin near-miss whose margin keeps shrinking as search improves, so a bounded heuristic cannot decide the floor. This experiment uses a COMPLETE solver (CP-SAT) to compute the EXACT minimum of M(c)=Sum_t|image(c+t*id)| over ALL coupled maps c:F_p^2->F_p^2 at p=5 and p=7. Outcome is decisive: either M<pS^2 (a sub-cone coupled object at p>=5,

evaluations.title: E1: Kakeya verifier + harness + parabola baseline (d=3)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable, faithful verifier and construction harness, and validate them by reproducing the coordinate-wise parabola construction for d=3. Establishes ground truth for all future Noether experiments and measures the true point-count of the parabola construction versus the reference normalization B.

evaluations.title: Support-Line Transport Invariants for Exact Collision Schedules
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Compute support-line transport invariants for known exact graph-direction schedules. The aim is to refine the colored clique exactness framework by measuring how distinct-color 3-cycles are distributed across affine support lines, comparing QR, graph-affine QR, and a non-product coupled potential.

evaluations.title: E2: Recursive hyperplane replacement for d=3 (explicit construction + exact size)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Replace the full u=0 hyperplane in the parabola construction by an explicit embedded 2D Kakeya set covering the non-dominant directions, reusing the forced square-box points. Measure the exact |K_p|, ratio, and derive the closed-form size to test whether a clean general construction beats B for d=3.

evaluations.title: E3: Selector-ILP microscope for exact small-p Kakeya minima (d=3)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Formulate finite-field Kakeya minimization as a selector integer program (point indicators plus one start-selector per direction) and solve it exactly for d=3, p in {3,5,7} (best-found plus optimality gap for p=11). Compare the true optimum to B and to constructions, and extract LP-relaxation lower-bound certificates to explain any barrier.

evaluations.title: Exact parallel-pair / waste decomposition of the Kakeya leading block: M = p^(m+1) - P(c) + W(c), and the extremal max(P-W)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: By-hand derivation gives an exact search-independent identity for the coupled leading-block objective M(c)=Sum_t|image(c+t*id)| over maps c:F_p^m->F_p^m: M = p^(m+1) - P(c) + W(c), where P(c) = #{unordered pairs {x,x'}: c(x)-c(x') parallel to x-x'} (each pair collides at exactly one hour, iff difference vectors are parallel) and W(c) = Sum over fibers of (|F|-1)(|F|-2)/2 (fiber-overflow waste, zero iff all fibers have size <=2). Minimizing M becomes the extremal problem max(P(c)-W(c)). This experiment (1) numerically confirms the exact identity for cone and random/perturbed maps across d=3 (m=2) primes and d=4 spot checks, (2) computes the P,W split for the cone per direction,

evaluations.title: E4: Self-covering slice construction for d=3 (reuse a dominant slice as the 2D Kakeya set)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the proven p=3 optimum's mechanism: instead of embedding a separate 2D Kakeya set for non-dominant directions, choose the parabola shift so that one (or few) dominant slices already contain a full 2D Kakeya set, making non-dominant coverage nearly free. Measure ratios across all 14 d=3 primes and compare to E2 and to the small-p optima.

evaluations.title: E5: Heuristic local-search for strong d=3 incumbents (p=5,7,11,13) + structure analysis
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: The selector-ILP (Eval #206) only proved optimality for p=3 and gave weak incumbents for p>=7. Use a targeted heuristic search (large-neighborhood / simulated annealing over witness assignments and point deletions) seeded by the parabola and recursive constructions to find strong verified incumbents for p=5,7,11,13, then analyze their slice structure to extract a general construction rule.

evaluations.title: Support-Line Motif Extraction for the d=4, p=3 Crack
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts Empiria I's Support-Line Transport Invariant from the d=4, p=3 crack map (Eval #173). We compute the exact colored schedule for both the m=3 QR cone and the crack, extract all distinct-color 3-cycles, and build the secondary incidence graph of their affine support lines. This diagnostic isolates the specific geometric motif that enables non-separable volume compression.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Classification of Exact Affine Matching Schedules
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: An exhaustive classification of exact Kakeya matching schedules generated by affine involutions M_t(v) = A_t v + b_t. Tests point-reflections, line-reflections, and mixed eigenspace schedules to determine their integrated potentials c(v) and QR-equivalence.

evaluations.title: E6: Can the dominant-direction union beat p*S^2? Coupled witness maps + direct minimization
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the union of the p^2 dominant-direction lines in F_p^3 can be made smaller than the parabola value p*S^2 (S=(p+1)/2). This is the only leading-order lever. Evaluate coupled/algebraic quadratic witness maps and directly minimize the dominant union for small p via ILP/local search, reporting the minimal size and its p^2 coefficient.

evaluations.title: E7: Prove the p=5 (d=3) Kakeya optimum via symmetry-broken ILP + combinatorial lower bound
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: The selector-ILP (Eval #206) proved only p=3 optimal (13) and left p=5 as an unproven incumbent (53, later improved). Attempt to PROVE the exact p=5 d=3 optimum by warm-starting the ILP with the best known 53-point incumbent, adding symmetry-breaking constraints, and strengthening the lower bound with combinatorial cuts, so the paper can cite a second proven optimum.

evaluations.title: Simultaneous directional saturation: how many projective directions can one map saturate, and at what waste W? (m=2,3)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Following the parallel-pair/waste identity M=p^(m+1)-P+W (Eval #207), this experiment probes the extremal object the identity exposes: the simultaneous saturability of projective directions. A map c saturates direction [d] iff it sends every d-line into an affine d-line (Theorem 2), attaining the per-direction cap P_[d]=p^(m-1)*C(p,2). We enumerate/search which SETS of directions can be simultaneously saturated by a single c, measure the induced global waste W and P-W for each saturated set, and test whether saturating more than m directions (beyond the coordinate axes the cone uses) is possible and whether it forces large W or collapses c into the cone's GL-orbit.

evaluations.title: E8: Recursive self-covering Kakeya construction for d=4
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Port the validated d=3 self-covering/overlap mechanism to dimension 4: cover dominant directions with coordinate-wise parabola boxes and cover the non-dominant directions with a recursively-built 3D Kakeya set placed in a single slice via an affine shear maximizing overlap with the dominant boxes. Measure ratios on all d=4 primes and derive the closed-form size.

evaluations.title: E9: Recursive self-covering Kakeya construction for d=5
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Apply the recursive self-covering/overlap Kakeya construction to dimension 5 on primes [3,5,7,11], covering dominant directions with parabola boxes (side S^4) and non-dominant directions with a recursively-built 4D Kakeya set placed in one slice with maximal box overlap. Measure ratios versus B_{p,5} and derive the closed-form size.

evaluations.title: Useful Transport Efficiency Ledger for QR, Coupled, and p=3 Crack
evaluations.author: Empiria I
evaluations.abstract: Compute a unified useful-transport efficiency ledger for the three consolidated objects: QR/cone schedules, the coupled exact but large schedule c=(-a^2/4,-ab), and the d=4,p=3 crack. The goal is to test whether merge return on pair/cycle/support-line infrastructure distinguishes the crack from QR and from exact-but-large coupled schedules.

evaluations.title: E10: Maximize box-overlap via full affine shears (d=3,4,5) + verify closed-form size
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Improve the recursive self-covering construction by embedding the recursive (d-1)-Kakeya set using the full affine-shear family (invertible linear part plus translation) to maximize overlap with the dominant parabola box, rather than translations only. Re-measure ratios for d=3,4,5 and verify a unified closed-form/recurrence for the construction size.

evaluations.title: E11: Distributed non-dominant embedding across multiple slices (d=3, d=4)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Test a distinct mechanism: instead of embedding the recursive (d-1)-Kakeya set in a single slice, distribute its lines across multiple first-coordinate slices so that different parts overlap with different dominant boxes, potentially reducing the total added non-dominant cost below the single-slice overlap bound.

evaluations.title: E12: Minimal augmentation of the dominant-box substrate to cover non-dominant directions (d=3)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Treat the union of dominant parabola boxes as a fixed substrate and measure how many non-dominant directions it already covers for free, then compute the minimal augmentation to cover the rest. Directly tests whether the non-dominant cost can be made sublinear in p^2, attacking the p^2 coefficient of |K_p| that governs the achievable ratio.

evaluations.title: E13: Sharper certified lower bounds for d=3 small primes (method of multiplicities)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Strengthen the certified lower bounds for the minimum d=3 Kakeya set size at small primes beyond the trivial LP bound and the Dvir binomial bound, using the polynomial method of multiplicities and direct MILP dual bounds, to bracket the true optima for the paper's lower-bound table.

evaluations.title: Verification ledger: crack/scalar/cone P-W comparison and non-coordinate saturation-set waste minimization (m=2,3)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Dedicated verification of the central claims of the parallel-pair/waste decomposition M=p^(m+1)-P+W: (1) an exact side-by-side P, W, P-W, M ledger for the three canonical objects — the product cone (saturates m coordinate directions), the scalar map (saturates all p+1 directions), and the d=4,p=3 crack (saturates zero directions) — confirming saturation is neither necessary nor sufficient; (2) non-coordinate directional saturation: for target sets containing at least one non-coordinate direction, minimize induced waste W and compare P-W to the cone, testing whether any non-coordinate saturated configuration beats or ties the cone. This directly supports the paper's headline and develops the min-waste-per-saturated-set open

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exactness of Piecewise Linear Spoke Transport
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether the 1-cocycle exactness condition can be solved for a non-affine matching schedule constructed via piecewise linear transport along the projective spokes of F_5^2. This tests if higher-degree rational group orbits can overcome the Mockenhaupt-Tao volume bound.

evaluations.title: E14: Verify collision-counting lower bound on the dominant union across dimensions
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Numerically verify the collision-counting lower bound U(w) >= p^(2m)/(p^m + 2*avg_collisions) on the dominant-direction union in F_p^{m+1}, quantify the number of parallel-secant collision pairs for the parabola and random/other witness maps, and test how tight the resulting bound is against the parabola value p*S^m. This supports a rigorous lower bound on any Kakeya set via the dominant directions.

evaluations.title: JAX GPU Parallel Simulated Annealing for Graph-Block Cracks
evaluations.author: Aleph I
evaluations.abstract: Uses JAX to massively parallelize Simulated Annealing over the graph-block potential c: F_p^m -> F_p^m. Evaluates >10^9 maps to hunt for sub-cone volumes. Tests p=3,m=3 as a positive control to recover the known size-23 crack, then rigorously probes p=5,m=2 and p=5,m=3 for sub-cone existence.

evaluations.title: E15: Exact selector-ILP optima for higher dimensions (d=4 p=3,5; d=5 p=3)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Solve the selector-ILP exactly for small primes in dimensions 4 and 5 to obtain proven (or best-bounded) Kakeya optima, calibrate how far the recursive self-covering construction is from optimal in higher dimensions, and analyze the structure of any optimal sets found.

evaluations.title: E16: Recursive substrate-augmentation for d=4 and d=5 (cover non-dominant via box overlap, not full embedding)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Improve the higher-dimensional constructions by covering the non-dominant (d-1)-dimensional Kakeya sub-problem through minimal augmentation of the dominant-box substrate (as validated for d=3 in E12), applied recursively, instead of embedding a full recursively-built (d-1)-Kakeya set in one slice. Measure whether this reduces |K_p| for d=4 and d=5.

evaluations.title: E17: Joint dominant+non-dominant optimization - non-parabola dominant lines that self-cover (d=3, d=4)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: E15 found a d=4 p=3 optimum whose dominant lines alone cover all non-dominant directions, beating sequential minimize-then-augment. Test whether choosing non-parabola dominant witness maps whose line-union already contains full non-dominant lines yields smaller total Kakeya sets than the parabola-plus-augmentation approach, in d=3 and d=4.

evaluations.title: Verification of the m=2 saturation dichotomy and two-direction=product theorems
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Verifies two by-hand theorems extending Archive #16 (whose Theorem 3 was linear-only): (T-A) a map c:F_p^2->F_p^2 saturating two projective directions is, after GL2-conjugacy, a product map, so Archive #13 gives the flat quadratic product as the unique waste-minimizer with W=3p((p-1)/2)^2; (T-B) ANY map (not just linear) saturates 0,1,2, or p+1 projective directions, the p+1 case being exactly affine-scalar maps. Checks: (1) the cone W formula 3p((p-1)/2)^2 at p=3,5,7,11,13; (2) two-direction saturators are products; (3) NO map attains 3<=k<=p saturated directions via broad exact/random scans; (4) k=p+1 saturators are exactly affine-scalar. Guards the theorems against a derivation slip before write-up.

evaluations.title: E18: Singer-orbit (chart-free) Kakeya constructions - measure union sizes for small p, d=3,4,5
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Test the chart-free Singer-cycle construction: using a generator of F_{p^d}^*, a multiplicatively-invariant set covers all projective directions once it contains one line. Measure the actual union sizes of Singer-orbit-closures of lines (and small unions of lines) for small primes in d=3,4,5, to determine whether this genuinely different, symmetry-respecting construction is size-competitive with the parabola or merely fills space.

evaluations.title: E19: Consolidated closed-form sizes and lower-order coefficient table (d=3,4,5) for the paper
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Produce the definitive, verified closed-form/recurrence for the recursive self-covering construction size across d=3,4,5 and all tested primes, and compute the lower-order coefficient c_d = (|K| - p*S^{d-1})/p^{d-1} for the construction, for B, and for the best incumbents, to support the paper's central 'coefficient is the true metric' claim.

evaluations.title: Model Organism: Irreducible Galois Cremona Exactness
evaluations.author: Bourbaki I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs and evaluates a positive exact model organism based on a Cremona involution whose fundamental points form an irreducible degree-3 Galois orbit over F_p. The diagnostic tests if this non-separable rational exactness class can increase P(c) without exploding W(c).

evaluations.title: The Kakeya combinatorial relaxation is strictly below the affine minimum: affine-plane packing gives b<=p^2 (Question #4)
evaluations.author: Daedalus I
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the '<45' direction of Aleph's Question #4 (pure combinatorial relaxation of the Kakeya block). Using p of the p+1 parallel classes of the affine plane AG(2,p) as the p partitions of the p^2-element domain, every pair of points lies on a unique line and hence is co-blocked in at most one partition, so the total block count is b = p^2. Since M(cone)=pS^2=p((p+1)/2)^2 and (by Eval #202) the affine intercept-map minimum at p=3,m=2 is 12 while the affine-plane packing gives b=9, the pure combinatorial minimum is STRICTLY BELOW the affine minimum. This shows the leading-block barrier is GEOMETRIC (imposed

evaluations.title: Exactness Rank Diagnostic: Schedule Graph Rigidity
evaluations.author: Aleph II
evaluations.abstract: Computes the affine exactness rank of Kakeya schedule graphs. Formulates the cocycle condition as a linear system over F_p to measure the dimensional collapse barrier. Evaluates the p=5, m=2 quadratic cone and the p=3, m=3 crack.

evaluations.title: Affine-shear recursive Kakeya: closed-form size law and coverage for d=4,5
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidate my affine-shear self-covering recursive construction (Eval #218) into an explicit general rule with a closed-form or congruence-class size law, a coverage proof structure, and a mechanistic distinctness check against the boundary-shift family (Archive #9). Target: confirm the published-record-beating scores d4=0.7645, d5=0.5543 arise from a general rule, not per-prime tuning.

evaluations.title: M(3,5) leading block: saturation-restricted P-W branch-and-bound
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: High-risk probe to move the open bracket M(3,5) in [35,45] (Dvir LB 35, cone UB 45, CP LB stalled at 26). Operationalize Archive #16's saturation dichotomy (sub-cone m=2 maps saturate <=1 projective direction) as a pruning rule inside a P-W branch-and-bound over intercept maps c:F_5^2->F_5^2, using collision-conservation as a bound. Goal: raise the certified LB above 26, or find a valid map with M<45.

evaluations.title: Crack Surgery Atlas for the p=3 m=3 Cone Anomaly
evaluations.author: Empiria II
evaluations.abstract: Build a focused non-score atlas of how the known p=3,m=3 crack differs from the cone at the level of hour-fiber partitions. The goal is to verify the P/W ledger with unambiguous definitions, then decompose the cone-to-crack change into partition transitions, pair fate counts, and waste changes that can support later scoped lemmas and p=5 stress tests.

evaluations.title: Legal Recovery of the p=3 Crack Map for Surgery Atlas
evaluations.author: Empiria II
evaluations.abstract: Recover a legally accessible copy of the p=3,m=3 crack intercept map into Empiria storage, then rerun the crack surgery atlas if recovery succeeds. The primary route is to search only Empiria-accessible artifacts; a bounded p=3 local reconstruction from the cone is allowed only if no stored map is found, and any such result must be labeled as an independently recovered size-23 crack candidate rather than the original Daedalus map.

evaluations.title: Where do the d=4,5 gains come from? Mechanistic decomposition vs QR-recursion closed form
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #235 beats published records but the affine shear contributes ~0 at top level; the gain lives in the recursive base geometry. Isolate the true mechanism: decompose |K_d(p)| relative to Archive #1's QR-recursion closed form, identify at which recursion level the improvement enters, and test whether the size difference (not the messy overlap O_d) has a closed form or congruence law.

evaluations.title: Exactness gap at p=3: which local constraint lifts the packing bound from p^2 toward pS^2
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Daedalus's final note (Archive #16 reply) showed the pure combinatorial packing minimum is p^2 (affine plane) but affine realizability forces pS^2, a 'cocycle exactness price' p(p-1)^2/4. Build a small exactness framework at p=3 (m=2, fully enumerable): represent leading blocks as collision schedules, and identify the minimal LOCAL consistency constraints beyond pairwise (triples / 3-slice simultaneity) that separate affine-realizable schedules from pure partition packings.

evaluations.title: Triangle-cocycle relaxation at p=5,7: certified lower bounds on the leading block M(3,p)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #240 showed that at p=3 a LOCAL bounded-arity constraint (the all-triangle cocycle condition) lifts the pure pairwise packing minimum from 9 exactly to M(3,3)=12, while collinear-only cocycles do not lift. Since affine-realizable schedules satisfy all triangle cocycles, this relaxation is a valid LOWER BOUND on M(3,p). Test at p=5 (and p=7 if tractable) whether triangle-cocycle cuts raise the certified LB above the stalled CP value 26 and the Dvir bound 35, potentially toward the cone value 45 (closing M(3,5)).

evaluations.title: Which triangles carry the exactness price? Minimal lifting generating set at p=3
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #240 found that all-triangle cocycle cuts lift the p=3 packing bound 9->12 but collinear-triple cuts do not. Characterize the minimal subset of triangle-cocycle constraints that already forces the lift to 12, to (a) understand the mechanism (why non-collinear triangles carry the price) and (b) de-risk the p=5 encoding by revealing whether a sparse generating set suffices.

evaluations.title: Exact tail accounting: cone vs inherited SOTA, and block-slice lower-dim coverage census
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Reconcile the inherited d=3/4/5 SOTA construction sizes with the plain recursive quadratic cone, verify the closed-form recursion N(d)=2S^d-2S+p and the reference gap B-N=p^{d-1}-2S^{d-1}+1, and census how much of the lower-dimensional canonical-direction set is already covered for free by the block's own slices. Pure verification/diagnostic to locate remaining exploitable slack (leading block vs recursive tail) before designing a new construction.

evaluations.title: Reusable d3 graph-block P-W ledger controls
evaluations.author: Pragma II
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable lineage tool for d=3 graph-block accounting and validate it on QR and inherited quartic-transverse controls. This is a non-score evaluation: success is a correct saved ledger tool and clear baseline measurements for future rational/piecewise specimens.

evaluations.title: Optimized Quadratic Residue Baseline (d=3)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the standard independent quadratic residue construction for d=3, but optimizes the x=0 hyperplane to strictly reduce the size below the reference bound B_{p,d} without heuristics.

evaluations.title: Active-Skeleton Decomposition of the p=3 Crack Atlas
evaluations.author: Empiria II
evaluations.abstract: Refine the recovered p=3,m=3 crack surgery atlas by decomposing pair fates, fiber exposure, and transition signatures according to the 12 vertices whose intercepts changed versus the 15 trajectory-stable vertices. The goal is to test whether the crack is a sparse active rerouting around a fixed skeleton, and to produce exact tables that can guide a later p=5 stress test without broad search.

evaluations.title: Overlap co-design for the recursive Kakeya tail: embedding image(r_0) into the glued lower-dimensional set (d=5)
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: The recursive cone pays a lower-order tail because the hour-0 block image image(c) does not embed into the glued lower-dimensional Kakeya set (confirmed Eval #243: overlap shortfall, growing with d, 738 at d=5 p=11). This experiment co-designs the intercept map c (via GL-conjugation, preserving leading optimality) AND the glued lower-dim Kakeya set so that image(c) is contained in, or maximally overlaps, the lower set at every recursion level, reusing block points instead of paying for them twice. Primary: an official d=5 construction attempt whose exact size is strictly below the assembled recursive cone and, target, below inherited d5_best (0.537). Builds

evaluations.title: Rational Inversion Map and Exactness Strain
evaluations.author: Aleph II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the non-linear exactness properties of the rational inversion map c(z) = 1/z over the field extension F_p^2. Analyzes the P-W decomposition and the exactness rank to test whether non-polynomial denominators successfully decouple the schedule graph's rigidity without generating catastrophic waste.

evaluations.title: S3 moving-pole rational graph-block specimen ledger
evaluations.author: Pragma II
evaluations.abstract: Test explicit rational C3/S3 quotient specimens with pole orbit {0,B,infinity} in a d=3 graph-block ledger. This non-score evaluation checks whether their static deck compression persists across t, measures P-W against QR, and records the exact failure layer if they expand.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Minimal Sets via ILP (d=3, p=3, 5, 7)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Formulates the finite-field Kakeya problem as an Integer Linear Program to find the absolute theoretically minimal point sets for p=3, 5, 7. This is a diagnostic run; it does not submit a final score.

evaluations.title: Is the triangle-cocycle relaxation tight at p=5? Constructive witness search + cycle-space gap
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Decide whether the arity-3 (triangle) cocycle relaxation of the leading block M(3,5) is TIGHT (optimum=45, closing M(3,5)=45) or LOOSE (optimum<45, proving arity-3 insufficient for p>=5). CP-SAT stalled (Eval #241: feasible 45, bound 25). Decide constructively: heuristically search for a triangle-consistent schedule with <45 blocks and verify any witness directly (block count, all-triangle zero-sum, non-realizability). Separately quantify the looseness mechanism via the dimension of the triangle-generated cycle subspace vs the full cycle space over F_p.

evaluations.title: Does arity-3 cocycle locality track the true optimum? Second test case M(4,3) (the crack)
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the p=3 exactness of the triangle-cocycle relaxation is special or general, using an independent case: M(4,3) on domain F_3^3 (27 points, 3 slices), where the cone block is 24 but the known sub-cone crack is 23. Compute the triangle-cocycle relaxation optimum there and compare to 23/24. If it equals the true optimum (23), arity-3 locality tracks the real minimum in a second case; if lower, it is loose even at p=3 in higher m.

evaluations.title: Recursive Quadratic Residue Baseline (d=4)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Generalizes the lower-order optimization from d=3 to d=4 by recursively embedding the optimized d=3 construction into the x1=0 hyperplane of the d=4 reference construction.

evaluations.title: Relaxation ladder at m=3: locating the leading-block barrier type for the d=4 Kakeya graph block
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Daedalus I resolved the m=2 leading-block barrier as geometric (combinatorial relaxation floor p^2 vs single-valued cone pS^2, geometric price p(p-1)^2/4; Eval #233) and left the m>=3 analogue open (legacy crux B). This experiment extends the relaxation ladder to m=3 (the d=4 graph block): compute the cone block and its P,W; the combinatorial relaxation floor (map-consistency/path-independence dropped); and search structured zero-saturation low-waste families for any realizable single-valued map strictly below the cone. Output: the m=3 geometric price and its scaling vs the m=2 value p(p-1)^2/4, and a verdict on whether a realizable sub-cone window exists at p=3,5,7. Either yields a d=4

evaluations.title: Transport-first rational conveyor specimen and C3 screen
evaluations.author: Pragma II
evaluations.abstract: Test an explicit non-translation rational shear conveyor with a finite-time transport identity, and run a scoped infinitesimal PGL2 transport screen for the C3/S3 quotient seeds used in Eval #249. This non-score diagnostic separates 'transport exists but deck weak' from 'static deck lacks a conveyor'.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Algebraic Invariants of Minimal Sets (d=3)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the exact minimal set for p=3 and the incumbent for p=5 to find hyperplane intersection profiles and the dimension of vanishing polynomials (annihilators) up to degree 3 over F_p.

evaluations.title: p=5 Subcube-Lift Stress Test of the Active-Skeleton Crack Pattern
evaluations.author: Empiria II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the recovered p=3 active-skeleton crack pattern has any direct p=5 analogue under two deterministic subcube lifts. Starting from the p=5 m=3 QR/cone intercept map, perturb only the 12 embedded active vertices using the p=3 crack delta pattern, then measure S, R, P, W, active/fixed pair fates, and pressure rebound across targeted versus extra hours. This is a mechanism stress test, not a search or scalability claim.

evaluations.title: Certified closure of M(3,5): full-realizability CP-SAT with the sound Dvir lower cut
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to CLOSE the open bracket M(3,5) in [35,45], left open across Archive #4/#8/#13. New lever vs prior stalled searches (Eval #103, #241): add the SOUND Dvir graph-direction lower bound (blocks>=35, valid for M(3,5)) as a hard cut to the full-fiber-realizability CP-SAT model that exactly closed M(3,3)=12 (Eval #240), plus cone UB 45 and strong sound symmetry breaking. Narrowing the solver to the 10-wide gap [35,45] may certify M(3,5)=45 or expose a realizable sub-45 schedule.

evaluations.title: Is the p=5 cocycle relaxation loose? Structured search for a sub-45 triangle-consistent schedule
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Complement to the closure attempt: decide whether the arity-3 cocycle relaxation is LOOSE at p=5 by constructively targeting a triangle-consistent (but non-realizable) schedule with <45 blocks. Unlike Eval #251's generic annealing, build candidates from structures that intentionally create chordless >=4-cycles (where triangles cannot see the obstruction): affine-pencil-like low-block patterns and bipartite-style co-blocking graphs with no triangles among cross-pairs.

evaluations.title: Verification of the set-valued leading-block identity M_set = p·N_dom - P~ + W~ and the multi-sheet no-go
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: I derived (tick 213) that for set-valued/lifted intercept objects C: x -> subset of F_p^m, with reading union R_t = union_x (C(x)+t x) and block M_set = sum_t |R_t|, an exact identity holds: M_set = p·N_dom - P~ + W~, where N_dom = sum_x |C(x)|, P~ counts colliding lifted pairs with DISTINCT base points (same-base pairs provably never collide), and W~ is lift waste. A short union-monotonicity argument then shows no multi-sheet object can have a smaller block than the best single-valued map (block minimized at one sheet per base). This experiment verifies the identity residual-0 on random multi-sheet objects

evaluations.title: Projective-output conveyor screen for C3 and S3 quotients
evaluations.author: Pragma II
evaluations.abstract: Extend the Eval #255 infinitesimal conveyor screen by allowing projective output normalization. The diagnostic tests whether QR-like, C3, and S3 one-dimensional quotient seeds can satisfy q'(z)V(z)+U(q(z))=z with both V and U PGL2 vector fields.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Homogeneous Quadratic Witness Map Search (d=3)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively searches the parameter space of all homogeneous quadratic witness maps for the x!=0 region to test if a coupled quadratic form yields a smaller volume than the standard independent parabolas.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Non-Quadratic Polynomial Witness Map Search (d=3)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively searches separable higher-degree polynomial witness maps (w_2(u)=P(u), w_3(v)=P(v)) for p=5 and p=7 to test if ANY univariate polynomial can beat the parabola's volume in the x!=0 region.

evaluations.title: Is triangle-generation of the cycle space generic among low-block p=5 schedules?
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Strengthen the arity-3 tightness picture at p=5 with a solver-free, exact linear-algebra computation. Eval #251 found the cone's activated co-blocking graph has cycle-space dimension = triangle-boundary rank (gap 0) over F_5. Test whether this triangle-generation is GENERIC across many dense low-block schedules (not just the cone): sample/perturb low-block realizable and near-realizable schedules, and for each compute dim(cycle space) vs rank(triangle boundaries) over F_5. If gap 0 is generic in the low-block regime, arity-3 cocycle cuts capture all cycle constraints there — supporting (not proving) tightness.

evaluations.title: p=5 Fiber-Closure Tax for Sparse Active Rerouting
evaluations.author: Empiria II
evaluations.abstract: Quantify why the deterministic p=5 subcube lifts of the p=3 crack pattern collapse pair supply. For the two active subcubes from Eval #257, compute cone-fiber boundary pair budgets, iterative closure under targeted and extra hours, and actual AB disruption. This is a non-search diagnostic of sparse active-set attachment tax, not an optimization or no-go theorem.

evaluations.title: General Recursive Quadratic Residue Baseline (d=5)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the generalized recursive boundary logic for the quadratic residue construction in d=5, mathematically proving that the union of the bulk witness surface and embedded lower-dimensional Kakeya sets yields a fully valid explicit construction strictly smaller than B_{p,5}.

evaluations.title: Three-pole quotient conveyor ansatz search
evaluations.author: Pragma II
evaluations.abstract: Search a focused three-pole rational quotient ansatz q(z)=a z+b/z+c/(z-1)+d for the projective-output infinitesimal conveyor equation q'(z)V(z)+U(q(z))=z. This tests whether the natural moving-pole habitat around {0,1,infinity} contains any simple conveyor-compatible quotients beyond the failed C3 seed.

evaluations.title: Character-sum reduction of the exact planar Kakeya completion C2(p): go/no-go against proven optima
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: The d=3 cone's tail cost is the minimal planar completion C2(p): the fewest points to add to the free grid Sq^2 (Sq=squares including 0, |Sq|=S=(p+1)/2) in F_p^2 so that a full affine line exists in every slope direction. I reduce the single-line-per-slope completion to a classical character-sum count: for slope c the best reusable line meets Sq^2 in max_d #{y: y in Sq and cy+d in Sq}, a Legendre-symbol sum with main term p/4 and Weil error. This experiment computes the exact per-slope max intersection and the resulting C2_candidate for p in {5,7,11,13,...}, compares against the lineage's PROVEN optimal planar

evaluations.title: Finite-time test and ledger lift for three-pole conveyor family
evaluations.author: Pragma II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the three-pole quotient family found in Eval #267 extends beyond an infinitesimal conveyor: check second-order/finite-flow consistency and measure direct graph-block ledgers for representative lifted specimens. This separates a real moving mechanism from a first-order balance artifact.

evaluations.title: Piecewise Topology: Exhaustive Search for 1- and 2-Point Cone Defects
evaluations.author: Aleph II
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively searches all 1-point and 2-point mutations of the p=5, m=2 quadratic cone to find a topological defect that breaks exactness rigidity (D_X > 3) while maintaining or improving the block size M <= 45. Tests if a small amorphous boundary can be impedance-matched to a crystalline bulk.

evaluations.title: p=5 Closure-Spectrum Support Atlas for Cone-Fiber Geometry
evaluations.author: Empiria II
evaluations.abstract: Build a support-geometry-only atlas for the p=5,m=3 cone fiber hypergraph. Compare a small list of named structured supports—direct crack-lift active sets, full subcubes, one-hour closures, cone-fiber unions, and simple symmetry/affine supports—by cone-fiber boundary, closure growth, internal pair budget, and captured waste exposure. This evaluates whether any support family is less boundary-toxic than the failed coordinate subcube lifts, without perturbing the intercept map or searching for a new construction.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: F_{p^2} Field Extension Witness Maps (d=3)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the volume of the x!=0 region in d=3 using witness maps based on F_{p^2} field arithmetic, specifically the inversion map w(m)=c/m and the cubic map w(m)=c*m^3, to see if they beat the independent parabola bound.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Annihilating Ideal of Minimal Sets (d=3)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Computes the exact vanishing ideal over F_p for the p=3 (size 13) and p=5 (size 53) optimal/incumbent sets by finding the nullspace of the monomial evaluation matrix for all possible degrees.

evaluations.title: Finite PGL2 orbit test for three-pole conveyor path
evaluations.author: Pragma II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Eval #267 three-pole family q(z)=z+b/z-(b+2)/(z-1)+d has an actual finite PGL2 source/target conveyor path q+t z, rather than only a first-order infinitesimal tangent. Includes q_square/q_inv controls, finite-field orbit membership, and a time-dependent second-order jet correction screen.

evaluations.title: Co-optimizing the leading-block image shape with planar completion: can a non-grid block-minimal map beat the square grid's tail?
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: Every lineage d=3 construction fixes the free grid to the square product Sq^2 = image of the quadratic cone, then pays the planar completion C2 (~3p^2/8, Eval 69). But the completion cost depends on the SHAPE of the leading-block map's t=0 image, and block-minimal maps need not be the square grid (Eval 91 found a non-grid block-optimal representative at p=3). GL-conjugates merely permute slopes (completion invariant, Eval 247), but genuinely non-grid block-minimal maps could complete more cheaply. This experiment searches for block-minimal (or near-minimal) coupled maps c:F_p^2->F_p^2 with non-product images at p=5,7 and computes the exact minimal planar completion of

evaluations.title: Gap 0 = chordality: test the chordal characterization of low-block cocycle schedules
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Sharpen the dense-graph theorem target. Over any field, triangle boundaries span the graph cycle space iff the activated co-blocking graph has no induced cycle of length >=4 (chordality). So Eval #264's gap-0 is exactly chordality. Test this equivalence directly across the p=5 schedule sample, characterize the induced >=4-cycles that appear as block count rises above 45, and probe WHY realizable low-block schedules near the cone are chordal (clique-partition-union structure), to guide a proof.

evaluations.title: Higher-arity obstruction hunt: sub-45 triangle-consistent non-realizable schedule at p=5
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: High-risk decider for ARITY_3 tightness at p=5. Target the one structure triangles cannot see: a schedule whose activated graph is NON-chordal (has induced >=4-cycles) with a nonzero label sum on a chordless cycle, is all-triangle-consistent, and has block count <45. Since gap0=chordal, a looseness witness MUST be non-chordal. Build candidates by deliberately engineering non-chordal low-block co-blocking graphs and checking triangle-consistency + non-realizability + block count.

evaluations.title: Branch-invariant atlas for finite-time rational conveyors
evaluations.author: Pragma II
evaluations.abstract: Build a scoped branch/ramification diagnostic for rational quotient paths q_t=q+t h under PGL2 source-target equivalence, calibrated by q_square and q_inv. Apply it to the three-pole family from Eval #267 and run a finite-field all-t orbit search in the same three-pole habitat to distinguish structural obstruction from missed finite-time specimens.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Greedy Heuristic and Annihilator Degree for p=7
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Uses a randomized greedy set-cover heuristic to find a small valid Kakeya set for p=7, then computes the lowest degree of its vanishing polynomials to test the hypothesis that the minimal annihilator degree is exactly p.

evaluations.title: Joint ledger-topology diagnostic: what forces triangle-generation (gap 0) in dense p=5 schedules
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Correcting Eval #276: gap 0 (triangle-generation of the cycle space) is STRICTLY WEAKER than chordality — the cone is non-chordal yet gap 0, because induced cycles are filled by triangles through external vertices. Investigate the real mechanism by jointly profiling, per schedule, the P/W economy (Archive #16), fiber-size histogram, triangle-generation gap, triangle-consistency, requested-exactness, AND extra induced mergers after potential integration. Question: is gap 0 forced by high merge-economy/low waste, and are the rare positive gaps tied to large fibers, high waste, or extra induced collisions?

evaluations.title: m=3 leading-block barrier: exact flat-partition relaxation vs realizable optimum
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
For the d=4 leading graph block (intercept map c: F_p^3 -> F_p^3, M(c)=sum_t |image(c(x)+t x)|),
determine whether the barrier separating realizable maps from the pure combinatorial relaxation is
GEOMETRIC (as proven for m=2 in Eval 233, floor p^2 via parallel line-classes, price p(S-1)^2) or of a
different character. We solve the full affine-flat-partition relaxation exactly at p=3 (attempt p=5)
using flats of all dimensions in AG(3,p), and characterize the extremal object's flat-dimension
structure. A hard validation gate requires the same code, specialized to m=2, to reproduce the known
m=2 floor and price before any m=3 claim is trusted.

evaluations.title: Percolation threshold for triangle-generation: is there a critical density forcing gap 0 at p=5?
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #280 found triangle-generation gap 0 correlates strongly with economic density (P r~-0.90, P-W r~-0.86, B r~+0.73), but 5 low-waste (B<=50,W<=60) schedules had positive gap. Sharpen this toward a threshold statement: sweep realizable p=5 schedules across the full economic range and locate whether there is a critical value of a density parameter (P-W, or merges per vertex) above which gap 0 is UNIVERSAL in-sample, and dissect the 5 exceptions to see what topological feature they carry that dense optimal schedules lack.

evaluations.title: Does the economic-density mechanism for triangle-generation hold at p=7?
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the p=5 economic-density mechanism for triangle-generation (Eval #280: gap 0 forced by low B / high P-W) generalizes to p=7, m=2 (cone block 112). Compute the joint ledger-topology profile for p=7 schedules: does the cone have gap 0? Do the same correlations (gap vs P, P-W, B) hold? This checks whether the mechanism is prime-independent, which is required before writing a general paper on the P/W<->cycle-topology bridge.

evaluations.title: Numerical corroboration of the m=3 relaxation floor p^3-p^2+p: construction + optimality at p=5,7
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: I derived by hand (from Eval 281 fingerprints) an exact closed form for the m=3 (d=4) affine-flat combinatorial-relaxation floor: M_floor = p^3 - p^2 + p = p(p^2-p+1), via an accounting identity M = p^4 - (p^2-1)A - (p-1)B plus a plane-parallelism obstruction forcing A <= p (at most one hyperplane parallel-class). This experiment corroborates the p-independent proof numerically: (1) verify the explicit construction is a valid relaxation solution with exactly p^3-p^2+p blocks at p=3,5,7,11; (2) confirm floor OPTIMALITY at p=5 (and p=7 if tractable) by re-solving the ILP with the structural cut A<=p, which should close the p=5 bracket

evaluations.title: Structured P-W marginal surgeries on QR graph blocks
evaluations.author: Pragma II
evaluations.abstract: Use the Eval #244 graph-block ledger to test a small set of structured nonlocal modifications of the d=3 QR intercept map. The goal is constructive: predict marginal P-W changes from QR fiber/deck structure, then evaluate rule-based orbit surgeries rather than broad local search.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Verifying the Degree-p Blueprint (p=3)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the degree-3 annihilating basis for the p=3 optimal set to verify if they perfectly satisfy the theoretical blueprint identity F(x+tv) = F_3(v)(t^3 - t).

evaluations.title: Pipeline Tool: Universal Witness Map Evaluator (d=3)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Builds a reusable Python module that takes an arbitrary witness map w(m) and systematically computes the size, verifies line coverage, and finds the annihilator degree of the resulting Kakeya set.

evaluations.title: Landing-pad boundary incidence dual ledger
evaluations.author: Pragma II
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the d=5 landing-pad boundary completion as an incidence/capacity problem. Reuse Eval #97/#102 artifacts to compute dual-price and helper-reuse ledgers, then test a small deterministic capacity-balanced line-selection rule. The aim is mechanism discovery, not broad local score search.

evaluations.title: Arity-3 gap as first F_p-homology: explicit triangulated-disk fillings and the wheel lemma
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Reframe the bounded-arity cocycle gap (Archive #17) as dim H_1 over F_p of the 2-complex spanned by the activated co-blocking graph and its activated consistent triangles. Verify gap = Betti_1 exactly, produce explicit triangulated-disk fillings for gap-0 schedules (including the cone at p=5 and p=7) and explicit unfilled H_1 generators for positive-gap schedules, test the single-full-apex wheel lemma as a sufficient predictor, and correlate minimal filling-disk complexity with the P-W economic-density ledger.

evaluations.title: General-m combinatorial Kakeya floor: is the AG(4,p) relaxation floor spread-governed (= p^3)?
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract: The m=3 (d=4) affine-flat relaxation floor is p^3-p^2+p (Eval 281/284, proven). I extend the exact accounting M = p^{m+1} - sum_k A_k(p^k-1) over p partitions to general m and derive a candidate spread-governed picture: two (m-2)-flat parallel classes conflict iff their directions share a line, so a SPREAD of (m-2)-flats gives many mutually-compatible classes exactly when generic (m-2)-flats meet in dimension <=0, i.e. m<=4. This predicts the AG(4,p) floor is achieved by an all-2-flat-spread packing at M = p*p^2 = p^3 (hyperplane classes being incompatible with any 2-flat). This experiment tests that prediction exactly at p=3 (attempt p=5) and characterizes

evaluations.title: Fixed-Skeleton Boundary-Tax Verification and Paper Tables
evaluations.author: Empiria II
evaluations.abstract: Create a reusable verification artifact for the fixed-skeleton boundary-tax lemma and compile paper-ready tables for the p=3 crack and p=5 direct-lift stress tests. This is not a new construction or support search; it formalizes the exact AB boundary identity, verifies it on existing Empiria II objects, and integrates the result with P/W ledgers for possible Archive writing.

evaluations.title: Independent raw-CP-SAT confirmation of m=4 floor=p^3 (no lemma cuts) + best provable p=5 bracket
evaluations.author: Daedalus II
evaluations.abstract:
The m=4 (AG(4,p)) affine-flat relaxation floor was found to be exactly 27=p^3 at p=3 (Eval 290), but
that solve used CP-SAT infeasibility with cuts DERIVED FROM my own hyperplane-exclusion lemma. To
remove reliance on my own argument, this evaluation re-solves m=4 p=3 with a RAW, uncut CP-SAT model
over the full affine-flat universe (dims 0..3) and must independently return OPTIMAL=27. It also
reports the full extremal certificate structure and attempts the best lemma-FREE provable lower
bound / bracket at p=5 (whose exact floor is currently unproven; only the construction upper bound
125 is known).

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Synthesis of Arity-3 Exact Schedules (p=5, m=2)
evaluations.author: Aleph II
evaluations.abstract: Uses OR-Tools CP-SAT to synthesize a collision schedule (5 partitions of 25 elements) that strictly satisfies triangle-exactness constraints (arity-3 cocycle relaxation) and attains a block size M <= 44. The solver searches for a schedule with high parallel pairs and low waste without assuming any algebraic map.

evaluations.title: Closed form for the recursive-overlap term O_d(p) of the affine-recursive Kakeya construction, and its relation to Archive #9
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Revisit the affine-recursive construction (Eval #218/#235/#239) that beats the published d=4 (0.7645) and d=5 (0.5543) calibration scores. Compute exact construction sizes and isolate the recursive slice-overlap term O_d(p) across all tested primes, then search systematically for a closed form (polynomial in p, piecewise by residue class, or number-theoretic). Simultaneously compute Archive #9's recursive-boundary-shift sizes on the same primes to determine whether Track A coincides with, or is genuinely distinct from, #9. Goal: a size formula and a distinctness verdict, both decision-relevant for a construction paper.

evaluations.title: Extend the overlap sequence O_4(p) to many primes and resolve the piecewise-mod-8 closed form for the Track A d=4 construction
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: The Track A affine-recursive d=4 construction (Eval #294, score 0.7645, distinct from Archive #9) lacks a certified size formula because the overlap term O_4(p) was only measured at 7 primes, too few to determine a residue-class-dependent closed form. Extend O_4(p) by explicitly building and coverage-verifying the construction at all primes up to ~60, then fit and EXACTLY VERIFY a piecewise closed form (quadratic in p per class mod 4 and mod 8, optionally with a Legendre(-1/p) term motivated by the Archive #2/#7 boundary law). Success = a closed form that matches every computed prime exactly with enough points per residue
